key_insight: A machine-learning pipeline using ADNI clinical, cognitive, and imaging-related data was built to detect early Alzheimer’s disease and highlight potentially important biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could support earlier identification of Alzheimer’s disease stages, helping clinicians monitor patients and plan care sooner.
method: Filled missing values with iterative imputation.
Balanced class imbalance using Borderline SVM-SMOTE and selected important features with wrapper/embedded methods.
Compared a stacking ensemble (Logistic Regression, Extra Trees, Bagging KNN, LightGBM) with an artificial neural network.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation with precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC on ADNI data after preprocessing and train-test splitting.
watch_item: Because the dataset comes from a specific research cohort and uses complex preprocessing, external validation is needed before real-world use.
paper_title: Predicting Early Stages Of Alzheimer's Disease And Identifying Key Biomarkers Using Deep Artificial Neural Network And Ensemble Of Machine Learning Methodologies
